cv-82eb6ab5.stem: What are the terminal branches of the popliteal artery?
cv-82eb6ab5.explanation: The popliteal artery divides at the lower border of popliteus into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries; the fibular artery arises from the posterior tibial artery.

cv-2167b2de.stem: Where is the posterior tibial pulse taken?
options: In front of the lateral malleolus
On the dorsum of the foot
cv-2167b2de.explanation: The posterior tibial artery is superficial between the medial malleolus and the Achilles tendon, where its pulse is taken.

cv-d0b5e87d.stem: Which is the largest vein of the body?
cv-d0b5e87d.explanation: The inferior vena cava carries the blood of all body parts below the diaphragm to the right atrium and is the largest vein of the body.

cv-ad43d739.stem: Which main vein brings blood from the head, neck and arms to the heart?
cv-ad43d739.explanation: The superior vena cava is formed by the union of the two brachiocephalic veins and brings blood from regions above the diaphragm to the right atrium.

cv-7aff291e.stem: Which is the longest vein of the body?
cv-7aff291e.explanation: The great saphenous vein is the superficial vein running along the medial side of the leg from the dorsum of the foot to the groin; it is the longest vein of the body.

cv-a4e595f7.stem: Which vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the digestive tract to the liver?
cv-a4e595f7.explanation: The portal vein carries blood from the stomach, intestines, spleen and pancreas to the liver; blood filtered by the liver returns to the IVC via the hepatic veins.

cv-eec7bdee.stem: Which structure prevents backflow of blood in veins?
options: Thick muscle layer of the tunica media
cv-eec7bdee.explanation: Valves, especially in the leg veins, make blood flow one way towards the heart. Valve incompetence leads to varicose veins.

cv-a92d99f7.stem: In which phase of the cardiac cycle do the coronary arteries fill most?
cv-a92d99f7.explanation: In systole the contracting myocardium compresses the coronary vessels; left ventricular coronary flow occurs mainly in diastole. That is why coronary perfusion falls in tachycardia, when diastole shortens.

cv-6061f2af.stem: Into which two branches does the left main coronary artery divide?
options: Anterior interventricular branch (LAD) and circumflex branch
Right marginal branch and circumflex branch
Sinuatrial nodal artery and atrioventricular nodal artery
cv-6061f2af.explanation: The left main coronary is a short trunk; it divides into the LAD, descending in the anterior interventricular groove, and the circumflex branch, which runs in the left AV groove around to the back of the heart.

cv-4e8377fa.stem: Where does the coronary sinus open?
cv-4e8377fa.explanation: The coronary sinus lies in the AV groove on the back of the heart, collects most of the cardiac veins and opens into the right atrium between the IVC opening and the tricuspid valve.

cv-428cedc8.stem: How do the semilunar (aortic and pulmonary) valves differ from the AV valves?
options: They have no chordae tendineae or papillary muscles.
They are not attached to the fibrous skeleton.
cv-428cedc8.explanation: Semilunar valves consist of three half-moon cusps that close when their pockets fill as blood starts to flow back; they have no chordae tendineae or papillary muscle support.

cv-77a5a53e.stem: The first heart sound (S1) is produced by the closure of what?
cv-77a5a53e.explanation: S1 is produced by closure of the AV valves at the start of ventricular systole, S2 by closure of the semilunar valves at the end of systole.

cv-dacff9e8.stem: From which aortic sinus does the right coronary artery arise, and in which groove does it run?
options: Right aortic sinus – anterior interventricular groove
Left aortic sinus – anterior interventricular groove
Left aortic sinus – left AV groove
Right aortic sinus – right atrioventricular (coronary) groove
cv-dacff9e8.explanation: The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus, passes between the right auricle and the pulmonary trunk into the right AV groove and runs around to the back of the heart.

cv-fcb9d64c.stem: At which level does the aortic arch begin and end?
cv-fcb9d64c.explanation: The aortic arch begins and ends in the plane through the sternal angle; this plane also corresponds to the tracheal bifurcation and the level where the azygos vein enters the SVC.

cv-d81fb0e2.stem: At which vertebral levels do the coeliac trunk, superior mesenteric artery and inferior mesenteric artery arise, respectively?
cv-d81fb0e2.explanation: The coeliac trunk arises from the front of the aorta at T12, the SMA at L1 and the IMA at L3; the renal arteries arise at L1–L2 and the bifurcation is at L4.

cv-1938d272.stem: Where do the gonadal (testicular/ovarian) arteries arise?
options: From the abdominal aorta, below the renal arteries (L2)
cv-1938d272.explanation: Because the gonads develop near the kidneys, their arteries arise high from the abdominal aorta and lengthen as the gonads descend. The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein.

cv-aeedc854.stem: Through which opening does the vertebral artery enter the skull?
cv-aeedc854.explanation: The vertebral artery ascends through the C6–C1 transverse foramina, winds over the posterior arch of the atlas and enters the skull through the foramen magnum.

cv-ae5c2252.stem: What is the main area supplied by the middle cerebral artery?
options: Lateral surface of the hemisphere (face and arm motor-sensory areas, language centres)
Medial surface of the hemisphere (leg area)
cv-ae5c2252.explanation: In MCA occlusion there is marked weakness and sensory loss of the opposite face and arm, with aphasia in the dominant hemisphere; the leg is less affected.

cv-81f7e82f.stem: In anterior cerebral artery occlusion, where is the paralysis most marked?
options: In the leg on the same side
In the leg on the opposite side
In the face on the same side
In the face and arm on the opposite side
cv-81f7e82f.explanation: The ACA supplies the medial surface of the hemisphere, including the leg area of the motor cortex; its occlusion causes marked weakness and sensory loss in the opposite leg.

cv-9199711f.stem: At the lower border of which muscle does the axillary artery become the brachial artery?
cv-9199711f.explanation: The axillary artery extends from the outer border of the 1st rib to the lower border of teres major, where it becomes the brachial artery.

cv-ac2759c4.stem: Which artery mainly forms the deep palmar arch?
cv-ac2759c4.explanation: The radial artery enters the palm through the 1st interosseous space to form the deep arch, which is completed by the deep branch of the ulnar artery. The superficial arch is mainly the ulnar artery.

cv-069cff78.stem: Which is the largest branch of the femoral artery in the thigh?
cv-069cff78.explanation: The profunda femoris arises about 4 cm below the inguinal ligament and is the main artery of the thigh muscles; it gives circumflex and perforating branches.
